ambiguities.text: The specification does not clarify what happens if a deposit with an invalid BLS signature is submitted - whether the ETH is permanently lost or can be recovered.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume ETH sent with invalid BLS signatures is effectively burned, as the beacon chain silently ignores invalid deposits but the execution layer contract has already accepted the ETH. This is consistent with the stated design that validation is deferred to the beacon chain.

ambiguities.text: The specification mentions MIN_DEPOSIT_AMOUNT but does not define its exact enforcement mechanism within the contract's Solidity/Vyper code.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the contract includes a require() or assert check against MIN_DEPOSIT_AMOUNT (1 ETH = 10^9 Gwei) and reverts if the amount is insufficient.

ambiguities.text: The withdrawal_credentials field has prefixes (BLS_WITHDRAWAL_PREFIX, ETH1_ADDRESS_WITHDRAWAL_PREFIX) but the contract does not validate the prefix byte.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume any 32-byte value is accepted as withdrawal_credentials by the contract, with semantic validation deferred to beacon chain processing. This allows future prefix types without contract upgrades.

implicit_assumptions.description: The deposit contract assumes the beacon chain will eventually process all valid deposits emitted as DepositEvent logs.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Deposits could be accepted and ETH locked in the contract without validators ever being activated, leading to permanent fund loss.

implicit_assumptions.description: The progressive Merkle tree assumes DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_TREE_DEPTH=32, supporting up to 2^32 deposits.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If the number of deposits exceeds 2^32, the Merkle tree would overflow, potentially corrupting the deposit root and preventing further deposits.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot front-run a legitimate deposit to change the deposit_data_root validation outcome.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If deposit ordering affects validation, an attacker could grief depositors by manipulating transaction ordering to invalidate deposit_data_root checks.
